name: Stratigraphy
desc: A subsiding basin writes its own record in cross-section — sea level rises and falls over minutes while sediment supply lags behind, so facies belts interfinger and march sideways across the plate, coal swamps drown into shale and shoal back into barrier sand, and every fall strips the top off in a truncation surface; the column scrolls downward forever, sagging into its syncline as it buries.

energy.doc: sediment supply rate (how fast the record accumulates) + colour/contrast gain

scale.doc: magnification into the section around x/y — 1 shows the whole column, 2.6 crops to a few beds

speed.doc: rate of geological time — how fast the column scrolls

density.doc: lithology ornament density: stipple, dashes, brick and coal partings

cycles.doc: sea-level swing: 0 = a quiet aggrading ramp, 1 = violent cyclothems with deep drownings and hard truncation surfaces

hue.doc: plate hue anchor; rotates the facies inks with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: survey = geological plate, facies colours + lithology ornament + inked truncation surfaces; core = wet grainy hand-sample, saturated, no ornament; seismic = abstracted red/blue wiggle-trace reflection section built from impedance contrast; xray = CT densitometry
